headline: A 2022 law raised school meal and child care food payments for the 2022-2023 school year and extended some COVID-19 food program waivers.
what_it_does: The law raises the federal reimbursement rate for school lunches by 40 cents and for school breakfasts by 15 cents starting in July 2022. It raises the reimbursement rate for meals and snacks in the Child and Adult Care Food Program by 10 cents, and moves tier II family or group day care homes up to tier I rates for 2022-2023. It also extends USDA's authority to waive certain program rules tied to COVID-19 on dates ranging from June 2022 to June 2023, and it cancels some unused funds from earlier COVID-19 laws.

who_it_affects.group: Public and private schools that take part in the National School Lunch and School Breakfast programs
who_it_affects.how: They receive higher federal payments for each lunch and breakfast they serve during the 2022-2023 school year.

who_it_affects.group: Child care centers and day care homes in the Child and Adult Care Food Program
who_it_affects.how: They receive a higher federal payment for each meal and snack, and tier II family or group day care homes are paid at tier I rates for 2022-2023.
Schools may keep certain COVID-19 meal flexibilities in place for a limited time, such as waivers tied to summer meals and food supply disruptions.
USDA must help them move back to normal school meal operations as COVID-19 waivers end.

who_it_affects.group: Agencies that had unused COVID-19 funds
who_it_affects.how: Certain funds previously given to USDA, the Department of Education, and the Small Business Administration are canceled.

when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on June 25, 2022; the rate increases apply to the school year beginning in July 2022, and waiver deadlines run from June 30, 2022 to June 30, 2023.
